episode.title: Replace unstable emoji-width markers in terminal-visible text
episode.before: At parent 52f875a875c20e927092a8b3aeb162614797543a, terminal-visible statuses, notices, summaries, and labels used emoji or emoji-presentation sequences such as 🟢, 🟡, 🔴, 🔄, ⏳, 🔎, 🚫, 💡, ✅, ❌, 🔒, and ⚠️. These strings could occupy two terminal columns or vary by renderer. Several state indicators also depended on color, and translated message keys and documentation embedded the old markers.
episode.after: At a756676b2180bd5ba8c0062f98f140c5f0a9e732, affected strings use narrower text-presentation symbols such as ✓, ✗, ◐, ●, ◌, ◎, ★, ▸, ▷, and ⚠, or omit redundant decorative prefixes. Connected, connecting, and disconnected IDE states have distinct text shapes independent of color. Locale keys and selected documentation are reconciled with the changed strings, while tests and snapshots assert representative rendered output and explicitly drive MCP connection states.
episode.diff: The implementation-bearing commit modifies 39 files with 251 insertions and 241 deletions. It replaces or removes emoji markers across CLI rendering, emitted session messages, and formatted agent statistics; strips U+FE0F from warning/info sequences; updates nine locale files and two user documents; revises unit assertions and Ink snapshots; and repairs MCP status tests so connecting and disconnected branches are selected through the component's serverStatus input instead of an ineffective module spy. The diff also changes some non-TUI strings, including retry-loop directives and PR attribution, so the change is broader than a purely terminal-rendering patch.

evidence_units.claim: Commit a756676b2180bd5ba8c0062f98f140c5f0a9e732 is linked to issue/PR 5999, has parent 52f875a875c20e927092a8b3aeb162614797543a, and records a 39-file implementation-and-test change intended to replace width-2 emoji with text symbols.
The parent rendered MCP states and startup/tip labels with 🟢, 🔄, 🔴, ⏳, and 💡; the pinned implementation uses ●, ◐, ◌, and ★ while retaining status-dependent color properties.
IDE connection output changes from colored-circle emoji to shape-distinct text markers: ✓ for connected, ◐ for connecting, and ✗ for disconnected, in both status formatting paths.

Terminal-facing markers are normalized across multiple semantic surfaces: redundant footer lock decoration is removed, workflow activity uses ▷, vision notices use ◎, blocked/error messages use ✗, tips use ★, pending work uses ◌, and statistics use text symbols such as ▸, ●, and ✓.
Warning and information markers remove the emoji variation selector, changing sequences such as ⚠️ and ℹ️ to text-presentation ⚠ and ℹ in user-visible messages.

The changed markers are consumed directly by Ink Text nodes, command message results, history items, session message emission, and statistics formatter return strings, making them observable at terminal-rendering or terminal-message call sites.

evidence_units.claim: All nine locale modules change affected translation keys and translated values alongside the source literals, including error, success, welcome, MCP startup, tips, and warning strings.

evidence_units.claim: User documentation removes the footer lock emoji and replaces documented IDE disconnection circle emoji, demonstrating that examples were considered part of the user-visible text contract.
IDE command tests assert exact ✓ Connected, ◐ Connecting, and ✗ Disconnected output, including disconnection details and the asynchronously emitted connected message.

MCP tests now inject DISCONNECTED and CONNECTING through the serverStatus prop, and snapshots verify ◌ startup, ● stable states, ◐ connecting output, and ★ tips. The connecting snapshot changes behaviorally from an incorrectly rendered Ready state to Starting output.
Additional tests assert the new ◎ vision marker, ⚠ text-presentation warnings, ◐ hook messages, ▸/●/✓/★ statistics text, and the complete ▷ workflow-active footer label.

The LSP table test expands its negative character class to reject both prior emoji and the newly adopted text markers, preserving that surface's plain-text status vocabulary rather than applying the glyph migration indiscriminately.
The retry-loop warning strings are explicitly documented as model-facing prompt directives rather than TUI glyphs, marking a semantic boundary even though their variation selectors are also removed.

The repository contains exact-output unit and snapshot oracles for representative connection states, notices, warnings, footer output, and statistics, but the available evidence bundle contains no CI status or recorded local test execution for the pinned commit.

candidate_atomics.name: normalize_terminal_visible_markers
candidate_atomics.title: Normalize terminal-visible markers to stable text symbols
candidate_atomics.description: Replace emoji and emoji-presentation sequences in terminal-visible strings with text-presentation symbols, or remove redundant decoration, while retaining the surrounding message and style semantics.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent status and message prefixes from consuming variable or unexpectedly wide terminal columns while preserving recognizable terminal output.
semantic_action.pre_state: Terminal-visible strings contain emoji, emoji-presentation variation selectors, or redundant decorative prefixes whose displayed column width can vary.
semantic_action.post_state: Affected terminal strings use the selected text-presentation marker or no redundant marker, with their substantive labels and formatting behavior retained.
semantic_action.validation: Assert exact rendered or formatted strings for representative components, notices, warnings, footer labels, and statistics output.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve_noncolor_state_distinctions
candidate_atomics.title: Preserve state distinctions without relying on color
candidate_atomics.description: Choose different text shapes for mutually exclusive states so status meaning survives NO_COLOR output, copy/paste, and color-vision limitations.

semantic_action.intent: Keep connected, transitional, and failure states distinguishable after replacing colored emoji.
semantic_action.pre_state: State meaning is encoded by colored emoji or by identical shapes distinguished mainly through color.
semantic_action.post_state: Each semantically distinct state has an independently recognizable text marker, with color remaining supplementary.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise every state branch and assert exact state-marker and label combinations; for IDE status the oracle is ✓ Connected, ◐ Connecting, and ✗ Disconnected.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile_embedded_text_contracts
candidate_atomics.title: Reconcile translations and documentation with changed display strings
candidate_atomics.description: Update localization lookup keys, translated values, and user-facing examples whenever the marker is embedded in the literal text contract.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent untranslated fallbacks and stale documentation after user-visible string literals change.
semantic_action.pre_state: Translations or documentation reference the old marker-bearing literal or rendered example.
semantic_action.post_state: Affected locale entries and selected documented examples correspond to the new display strings.
semantic_action.validation: Compare changed source literals against locale keys and inspect documented terminal examples for obsolete markers.

candidate_atomics.name: exercise_render_states_through_supported_inputs
candidate_atomics.title: Exercise rendered states through supported component inputs
candidate_atomics.description: Drive each status branch through the component's real injected state boundary and snapshot the resulting terminal frame, repairing tests that previously mocked an ineffective lookup.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure rendering tests actually cover the state-specific marker branches they claim to validate.
semantic_action.pre_state: A rendering test claims to cover a state but its mock does not affect the component's active state source, so the snapshot remains on the default branch.
semantic_action.post_state: The test supplies the desired state through the supported input and the snapshot demonstrates the corresponding rendered branch.
semantic_action.validation: The connecting MCP fixture produces ◐ and Starting text, while explicit disconnected input selects the disconnected branch rather than silently retaining the default status source.

candidate_atomics.name: guard_surface_specific_glyph_policy
candidate_atomics.title: Guard surfaces that must remain glyph-free
candidate_atomics.description: Keep text-only output surfaces from inheriting the terminal glyph vocabulary by asserting that both legacy emoji and replacement symbols are absent.

semantic_action.intent: Avoid applying a terminal marker migration to surfaces with a different output contract.
semantic_action.pre_state: A broad glyph replacement could introduce status symbols into a table, prompt directive, or other surface whose contract differs from interactive terminal status rendering.
semantic_action.post_state: Excluded surfaces retain their own vocabulary, with tests or comments making the boundary explicit.
semantic_action.validation: Use negative assertions for glyph-free output and explicit ownership comments for strings that are not terminal-rendered.

candidate_workflows.name: stabilize_unicode_markers_in_terminal_output
candidate_workflows.title: Stabilize Unicode markers across terminal output contracts
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for replacing width-unstable emoji in terminal-visible output without losing state meaning, breaking translations, or creating tests that fail to exercise the intended rendering branches.

workflow_graph.goal: Make affected terminal-visible markers occupy the intended text-style columns while preserving semantic state recognition and synchronizing dependent text contracts.
when_to_use: Terminal alignment, wrapping, or spacing is unreliable because user-visible prefixes contain emoji or emoji-presentation sequences.
A status interface uses colored emoji whose width or meaning changes across terminals, CJK environments, NO_COLOR output, or copied text.
Changing a rendered marker also changes localization keys, snapshots, exact-string tests, or documented examples.
anti_goals: Do not replace every Unicode character merely because it is non-ASCII.
Do not make state meaning depend only on color or use one identical shape for semantically opposed states.
Do not alter substantive labels, state transitions, or business behavior while repairing marker width.
Do not propagate the terminal glyph vocabulary into tables, model prompts, web-only text, or other surfaces without verifying their separate presentation contract.
Do not treat updated snapshots alone as proof when the fixture does not actually select the intended state branch.
not_applicable_when: The defect is caused by an incorrect width-calculation algorithm for arbitrary user content rather than fixed application-owned markers.
The output target is not a terminal and its renderer intentionally supports emoji presentation.
No implementation, call site, or test oracle can establish which strings are terminal-visible.
The marker is user-provided content that must be preserved verbatim.
inputs: Pinned implementation ref and parent ref
Inventory of application-owned marker-bearing strings and their rendering call sites
Locale catalogs, exact-string tests, snapshots, and documentation containing affected literals
List of output surfaces that must remain glyph-free or are not terminal-rendered
workflow_graph.entry_state: Application-owned terminal strings contain width-variable emoji or presentation selectors, and dependent state mappings or textual contracts still encode the old markers.
workflow_graph.exit_state: In-scope terminal strings use approved text-presentation symbols or no redundant marker; distinct states remain recognizable without color; affected translations, tests, snapshots, and documentation are reconciled; excluded surfaces retain their own output policy.

steps.condition: Apply only to application-owned strings confirmed to reach terminal rendering or terminal-visible message output.
steps.validation: Inspect final call sites and exact-output tests to confirm each old marker is replaced or removed without changing its substantive label.

steps.condition: Required whenever multiple semantic states previously relied on different colors or colored emoji.
steps.validation: Each state branch yields a distinct text shape and label; IDE tests assert ✓, ◐, and ✗ for connected, connecting, and disconnected states.

steps.condition: Classify adjacent output surfaces before applying replacements broadly.
steps.validation: Glyph-free surfaces have negative assertions, and non-terminal strings have explicit ownership or are deferred from terminal-width reasoning.

steps.condition: Run when markers are embedded in translation keys, translated values, user documentation, or external examples.
steps.validation: Affected locale keys and documented examples no longer rely on the superseded marker, subject to recorded documentation discrepancies.

steps.condition: Use the actual dependency-injection or prop boundary consumed by the renderer for every representative state.
steps.validation: Rendered frames or exact strings prove that stable, transitional, and failure branches emit their intended markers and labels.

validation_ladder: Diff-level audit: compare the parent and pinned ref for known emoji, U+FE0F sequences, and redundant decorative prefixes in application-owned terminal strings.
Call-site validation: confirm changed literals flow into terminal Text nodes, terminal message objects, or terminal formatters rather than assuming from filenames.
Semantic validation: verify opposed and transitional states have distinguishable shapes independent of color.
Contract reconciliation: check locale keys, translated values, exact-string assertions, snapshots, and documented examples.
Branch-realism validation: drive stateful renderers through the input they actually consume and inspect the resulting frame.
Execution validation: run the targeted unit and snapshot suites when the checkout and dependencies are available; no execution result is present in this evidence bundle.
stop_conditions: Stop if the string cannot be shown to reach a terminal-visible surface and no separate output contract justifies changing it.
Stop if the proposed replacement is East Asian Ambiguous or otherwise lacks the required column-width behavior for supported terminals.
Stop if distinct states become distinguishable only through color.
Stop if a snapshot fixture continues to render the default branch instead of the state named by the test.
Defer completion if translation keys or public examples cannot be reconciled with the final implementation.
unresolved_or_deferred: No CI status, test command output, or local successful test run is available in the supplied evidence.

The change contains no direct wcwidth-style or multi-terminal column measurement test; width-one behavior is asserted by implementation choice and exact rendered text rather than measured across terminal implementations.

docs/users/ide-integration/ide-integration.md documents disconnected IDE messages with ●, while the final implementation and unit tests use ✗; that documentation discrepancy remains unresolved by the pinned commit.
The squash commit message contains intermediate claims that conflict with parts of the final diff, so final-tree evidence was preferred.
The final diff also alters non-terminal strings such as model-facing retry directives and PR attribution; their behavioral necessity for terminal-width repair is not established.

unresolved_questions: Were the targeted CLI and core test suites or CI checks successful for the pinned commit? The GitHub bundle explicitly lacks status-check metadata.
Was the IDE integration documentation's ● Disconnected marker intentionally different from the final ✗ implementation, or is it a stale review artifact?
Are ●, ◐, ◌, ◎, ★, ▸, ▷, ✓, and ✗ guaranteed single-column under every terminal and locale officially supported by the project? No cross-terminal width test is present.
Why does the final diff remove 🤖 from PR attribution and strip variation selectors from model-facing directives even though those strings are not established as TUI-rendered?
